findings_qualitative.value: CO(3-2) clumps form kinematically distinct filaments; Streamer and Southern filament appear infalling

evidence.quote: Some of the filaments appear to be falling into the galaxy and may be fueling its current star formation.

findings_qualitative.value: CO clumps anti-correlated with Halpha but correlated with radio free-free

evidence.quote: are anti-correlated with H$\alpha$ on $\sim$5 pc scales, but are well-correlated with radio free-free emission

claims.hypothesis: Is the dense gas organised in kinematically distinct filaments, and are they infalling?
claims.experiment: MOM0 and MOM1 of 12CO(3-2) at 0.3 arcsec
claims.result: Streamer ~20-40 km/s red, Cloud F 20-30 km/s blue, Southern filament ~50 km/s red of v_sys 380
claims.finding: Filaments are distinct; Streamer and Southern filament likely infalling, Cloud F infalling on far side

evidence.quote: Thus, each filament is distinctly defined kinematically and spatially, formed of gas that is sufficiently dense to form stars.

claims.hypothesis: Is Cloud D1 optically thin in CO(3-2)?
claims.finding: D1 and D2 may be optically thin, possibly because hot

evidence.quote: We propose that Clouds D1 and D2 are most likely optically thin in CO(3–2) because the molecular gas is hot

claims.hypothesis: Is star formation in Cloud D1 unusually efficient?
claims.experiment: Compare gas mass with SFR from radio continuum
claims.result: tau_dep ~8 Myr, ~100 times shorter than typical low-metallicity galaxy
claims.finding: Star formation in D1 is extraordinarily efficient

evidence.quote: This star formation is unusually efficient.

evidence.quote: the $\sim$4$''$ $\times$2$''$ beam of the SMA images does not separate the dense gas at the cluster scale.
